facts.statement: Fossils of Ilokelesia were found in the Early Cretaceous Huincul Formation in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: preserved in layers of the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Huincul Formation (Neuquén Group) in Neuquén Province, Argentina

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Ilokelesia was described by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado in late 1998.
facts.quote: The only known specimen, consisting of fragmentary elements of the skull and skeleton, was described by Rodolfo Coria and Leonardo Salgado in late 1998

facts.statement: Ilokelesia is known only from very fragmentary skull, axial, and appendicular skeleton elements discovered in 1991.
facts.quote: Ilokelesia is only known from very fragmentary elements of the skull and the axial and appendicular skeleton, discovered in 1991

facts.statement: The Ilokelesia fossils were discovered ten meters away from the holotype of Huinculsaurus.
facts.quote: It was discovered ten meters away from where the holotype of Huinculsaurus was discovered

facts.statement: The species name aguadagrandensis refers to the locality Aguada Grande where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: while the specific name reflects the name of the locality where the fossil was found, Aguada Grande

facts.statement: Ilokelesia was a medium-sized theropod dinosaur.
A 2016 analysis estimated Ilokelesia to be 5.3 meters long.
facts.quote: In 2016 it was estimated to be 5.3 m in length in a comprehensive analysis of abelisaur size

facts.statement: Ilokelesia is characterized by distinctive features in the quadrate and postorbital skull bones.
facts.quote: It is characterized by features of the skull, namely of the quadrate and postorbital bones

facts.statement: Ilokelesia has distinctive vertebral features, including reduced processes on cervical vertebrae and dorsal vertebrae lacking pleurocoels.
facts.quote: The vertebral series also has distinctive characters setting it apart from other abelisaurs, such as reduced processes on the cervical vertebrae and dorsal vertebrae lacking pleurocoels

facts.statement: A subsequent analysis placed Ilokelesia within Abelisauridae as a brachyrostran carnotaurine.
facts.quote: A subsequent analysis has placed it within Abelisauridae, as a brachyrostran carnotaurine

facts.statement: Ilokelesia lived in South America during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 98 to 90 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 98 y 90 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense y el Turoniense, en Sudamérica

facts.statement: Ilokelesia is classified in the family Abelisauridae.
The fossil record for Ilokelesia spans from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)
